assumptions: Finite known loss and feedback matrices; bounded finite losses. Outcome distribution p fixed but unknown, iid across rounds in the stochastic branch.
K is the number of Pareto-optimal actions after duplicate loss rows are identified.
statement.conclusion: Minimax expected regret is 0 for K=1; soft-Theta(sqrt(T)) for K>1 and local observability; Theta(T^(2/3)) for global but not local observability; Theta(T) without global observability.
statement.objects_and_definitions: A finite known game (L,H), N actions and M outcomes; row losses ell_i, signal matrices (S_i)_{a,j}=1{H_ij=a}. C_i={p in simplex:ell_i^T p<=ell_j^T p for all j}. Empty cells are dominated; nonempty cells properly contained in another cell are degenerate; remaining actions are Pareto-optimal. Duplicate loss rows are identified for K. Two Pareto actions are neighbors if their cells intersect in dimension M-2. N_ij^+={k:C_i intersect C_j subset C_k}. Global observability: every ell_i-ell_j lies in sum_k im(S_k^T). Local observability: for every neighboring pair ell_i-ell_j lies in sum_{k in N_ij^+} im(S_k^T).
statement.parameter_domains: Asymptotic T->infinity; constants and hidden logarithms depend on the fixed game.
statement.quantifiers_and_randomness: For each fixed finite game; the worst-case iid distribution may depend on T.
